ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, one can see a gray cube, with the top being a light-colored face, and a small cube-shaped notch dug out near one corner. This notch reveals three mutually perpendicular internal small square faces; although the original outer side faces of the cube have been dug into notches and become concave shapes or corner-missing shapes, they still respectively belong to the original outer surfaces. Reasoning: The problem extends this operation in the figure to the second cube with side length 3 cm: at each of the 8 corners, dig out a small cube with side length 1 cm. The original cube has 6 outer surfaces. Each time a small cube at a corner is dug out, 3 mutually perpendicular small square inner surfaces are newly exposed, so the 8 corners add a total of 8 × 3 = 24 faces. Because the side length of the large cube is 3 cm, and only 1 cm is cut off at each corner, the cuts at adjacent corners will not connect together; each original outer surface is still a connected corner-missing face. Therefore the total number of faces is 6 + 24 = 30.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: it shows a 3 cm cube with a 1 cm cube-shaped notch removed from one corner; the notch visibly creates three new square inside faces while the old outside faces become notched but remain faces. From the text, transfer this operation to the second cube, where the same 1 cm cube is removed at all 8 corners. Start with the 6 faces of the original cube. Each removed corner cube exposes exactly 3 new mutually perpendicular square faces. Since the cube side is 3 cm and each corner cut is only 1 cm, cuts from adjacent corners do not merge; each original side remains one connected notched face. Thus total faces are 6 + 8 × 3 = 30.
